_comment: Unified configuration for both Claude Code and OpenCode — production-quality code with optimized token usage
_usage: Referenced by opencode.json and used natively by Claude Code

notes: Limit to 6 files per context to stay within token budget
Use Grep/Glob to find relevant files before reading
Load standards files lazily based on task type
Always name constraints explicitly
Always include created_at/updated_at/created_by/updated_by
Use parameterized queries only — no string concatenation
Prefer CTEs over nested subqueries for readability
Always include rollback in migration scripts

eslint_rules: Prefer type over interface for unions
Use optional chaining for nullable values

examples.api_call:
const response = await apiClient.get<UserResponse>('/users');
return UserSchema.parse(response.data);

notes: No 'any' type — use 'unknown' with type guards
Prefer type over interface for unions/intersections
Use Zod for runtime validation of API responses
All async functions: explicit error handling
Use React Server Components where no interactivity needed
Client components: 'use client' directive required
All forms: React Hook Form + Zod schema validation
CRITICAL: Follow .prettierrc.json (2-space indent, 100 char line)
CRITICAL: Validate with ESLint before submitting code

critical_rules: No 'any' type - use 'unknown' with type guards
Single quotes for TS code, double quotes for JSX attributes
Explicit error handling in all async functions
Zod validation for all API responses

always_enforce: No console.log in production code (use logger)
All API endpoints documented in OpenAPI spec
All public functions have JSDoc (TSDoc style)
Error responses follow RFC 7807 Problem Details
All DB queries use parameterized statements
Correlation ID propagated through all layers

notes: ALWAYS read project-structure.md before any file operations or directory navigation to avoid token waste on failed attempts
Load standards files only when relevant to current task
ALWAYS load typescript-formatting-standards.md before generating TypeScript/React code
Prefer targeted file reads over loading entire directories
Use search tools to find relevant code before reading whole files
Split large features into epics to stay within token limits

auth.mechanism: NestJS JwtAuthGuard (passport-jwt + jwks-rsa) on the Fargate service behind an internal ALB

network.note: All AWS SDK calls assume VPC + DirectConnect — no public endpoints

ui_library.note: Use the component library configured for this project. Check @.claude/project-structure.md.
ui_library.never_mix: Do not introduce a second UI component library without user confirmation

compliance: PCI DSS — where payment data involved

fargate.compute: Long-lived ECS Fargate service behind an internal ALB
fargate.batch: Scheduled ECS tasks via EventBridge Scheduler → RunTask (Murex EOD export, CMDM daily sync)
notes: Internal ALB (no public endpoints) routes Authorization: Bearer to the service
JwtAuthGuard (global) validates JWT via passport-jwt + jwks-rsa in-app
Use @RequirePermissions for method-level scope enforcement
Use RDS Proxy for connection pooling across service tasks and scheduled batch tasks
Warm containers (desiredCount >= 1, target-tracking autoscale) — no cold starts on the hot path
Use RDS Proxy for connection pooling behind the Fargate service and scheduled tasks
Enable Performance Insights
Automated backups: 7 day minimum retention

file_templates.note: Templates are in .claude/templates/ — load on demand

avoid_over_engineering: Don't add features beyond what was requested
Don't refactor code unless explicitly asked
Don't add docstrings/comments to unchanged code
Don't create abstractions for single-use operations
simplicity_principles: Only validate at system boundaries (user input, external APIs)
Trust internal code and framework guarantees
Don't add error handling for impossible scenarios
Delete unused code completely (no commenting out)
